events.text: Create a minimal but complete browser Snake game in a single self-contained snake.html file (inline CSS + JS, canvas, no external assets or libraries). Just create the file.
Add arrow-key and WASD controls and a visible score in the top-left.
Add pause/resume on the spacebar and a restart button below the canvas.
Make the snake speed up a little every 5 points.
Add a start screen with three difficulty buttons: Easy, Normal, Hard.
Add an optional wall-wrap mode toggled by a checkbox on the start screen.
Persist the high score in localStorage and show it next to the current score.
Before coding more, explain in prose the options you'd consider for mobile controls. Give a numbered list and end by asking which I'd like — but do not open any interactive menu, just plain text.
Add on-screen touch controls (swipe or buttons) for mobile, your choice from that list.
Add a sound on/off toggle using only the Web Audio API — no external sound files.
Refactor the JS into clear functions (input, update, render, state) inside the same file; keep it one file.
There's a bug: pressing the opposite direction quickly reverses the snake into itself. Describe the cause, then fix it.
Make the canvas responsive so it scales to the window while staying square.
Think hard about the best data structure for the snake body (array vs linked list vs deque) for this game, weigh the tradeoffs, and explain your reasoning before changing anything.
Summarize everything that changed and give exact steps to open and play snake.html.
